title: Long RTX — Patriot/THAAD Interceptor Emergency Replenishment
entry: Initiate $172-178 (current zone; June 3 morning). Scale: 70% at open; 30% add on any intraday dip to $170-172. Do NOT initiate above $180 — the geopolitical news is live and the stock gaps fast on Iran headlines.
stop_loss: $162 daily close (~7.5% below entry midpoint $175) — implies a formal Iran ceasefire is announced OR DoD emergency supplemental procurement is cancelled/delayed beyond Q3
targets: $190 — media confirms PAC-3/THAAD interceptor emergency procurement order submitted to RTX; Gulf-state Patriot upgrade contracts awarded (Kuwait, Bahrain, UAE); +8.6%
$205 — DoD FY2027 emergency supplemental request formally includes missile defense inventory rebuild; international Patriot PAC-3 MSE upgrade orders formalized with RTX guidance raise; +17.1%
$215 — full conflict duration premium expansion: operations extend beyond 60 days, triggering DoD multi-year procurement authorization; RTX backlog hits new all-time high; +22.9%
catalyst: Iranian drones severely damaged Kuwait International Airport on June 3 and Iranian missiles struck Bahrain simultaneously; US Central Command footage shows Patriot PAC-3 batteries engaging Fateh-110 ballistic missiles over Kuwait, with at least three interception attempts visible. US military data from early in the Iran conflict showed 150 THAAD interceptors expended in the first 12 days of kinetic operations — approximately 25% of US inventory. RTX manufactures PAC-3 MSE interceptors and co-produces THAAD kill vehicles. With Iran now projecting force horizontally against Gulf state civilian infrastructure (airports, ports, tankers) rather than solely threatening the Strait, the DoD emergency replenishment thesis has a new and concrete trigger. RTX is -19% from its March 2026 52-week high of $214.50 despite the war continuing, creating an entry at a meaningful discount to the prior conflict-premium high.
thesis:
RTX occupies the most irreplaceable position in the active-conflict supply chain: it makes the interceptor missiles — the expendables — not just the launchers. Lockheed Martin makes the THAAD system; RTX makes the THAAD kill vehicle and manufactures the PAC-3 MSE interceptor (the projectile fired from the Patriot launcher). When a Patriot battery fires three times at a single Fateh-110 missile over Kuwait, three PAC-3 MSE interceptors are consumed and must be replaced. At $3-4M per PAC-3 MSE round, the DoD is burning through inventory at a rate that requires emergency procurement at scale. Kuwait, Bahrain, Saudi Arabia, and the UAE all operate US-built Patriot systems — each allied nation's depleted inventory creates a parallel international order pipeline.

RTX entered June 2026 at $174, down 19% from its March 2026 high of $214.50. The markdown happened as the market initially priced in the Iran war premium in March and then partially de-rated as the conflict appeared to stabilize. The June 3 Gulf-state kinetic escalation resets the clock: Iran is no longer a Hormuz blockade holding pattern but an active offensive force striking civilian infrastructure across multiple Gulf states in a single 24-hour window. The DoD supplemental process (emergency procurement outside normal budgeting) is now politically and militarily justified. RTX Q2 FY2026 earnings (late July) will be the first formal confirmation of order intake acceleration — but the DoD press releases and RTX material disclosures should arrive within the 4-8 week horizon.

The bear-counter-party is the analyst who notes RTX's -19% decline from highs reflects awareness that production throughput — not demand — is the binding constraint. RTX can only manufacture PAC-3 MSEs at a limited monthly rate; emergency orders get prioritized but the revenue recognition lags 18-24 months. This is real: RTX stock can get ahead of deliveries. However, the market re-rates on ORDER intake (backlog) and the guidance RAISE that comes with emergency procurement authorization, not on delivery timing. The 4-8 week horizon captures the announcement effect, not the fulfillment cycle.

This position is distinct from existing defense longs: LMT is a precision-strike play (JASSM-ER, F-35); NOC is a strategic-systems play (B-21, ISR). RTX is the terminal-defense/interceptor play — the specific part of the defense supply chain being actively consumed in real time by Gulf-state Patriot engagements.
bull_case: DoD formally requests emergency PAC-3 MSE and THAAD kill vehicle procurement in the June-July supplemental; Kuwait, Bahrain, and UAE each place emergency Patriot upgrade orders concurrent with DoD. RTX Q2 earnings raise FY2026 guidance by 8-12% on order intake acceleration. Stock re-rates toward $205 (Target 2) within 5 weeks. Tail: Saudi Arabia orders 500+ additional PAC-3 MSE interceptors and announces a Patriot system expansion as Iran attacks become systematic.
bear_case: US-Iran ceasefire is announced within one week; Gulf-state kinetic attacks are attributed to a rogue IRGC unit rather than directed Iranian state policy; Trump confirms talks are live. RTX gives back the conflict premium; DoD supplemental is shelved. Stop at $162 triggered within 10 days. Structural: RTX's production capacity constraint means even large order announcements have no near-term revenue impact, limiting the multiple re-rating.
invalidation: $162 daily close, OR formal Iran ceasefire announcement with Hormuz opening timeline confirmed, OR RTX Q2 earnings guidance disappoints on interceptor segment revenue below $3B quarterly
